misconception_description: Student believes that while loops execute their body only once if the condition is true.

solutions.generated_code:
program SaringKataPanjang
kamus
  n, m, i, panjangKata : integer
  kata : string
algoritma
  input(n, m)
  i <- 1
  while i <= m do
    input(kata)
    panjangKata <- panjang(kata)
    if panjangKata > n then
      output(kata)
    endif
  endwhile
endprogram

metadata.modification_notes: The student replaced the for loop with a while loop but didn't include the loop counter increment (i += 1) because they believe the while loop will only execute once if the condition is true. From their perspective, the while loop should check if i < len(txt), execute the body once to check the first word, and then stop - similar to how an if statement works. They don't realize that the while loop will continue to check the condition and re-execute the body indefinitely, causing an infinite loop since i never changes. The student genuinely thinks this will work correctly to check the word at index 0 and then move on to return the result.
